panels.title: The piece (P00), verbatim
panels.detail:
Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.

The opening line of Tolstoy's Anna Karenina (Garnett translation). Not the author's writing.

tests.evidenceNote: P04 (fresh audit, interim prompt; not the fixed Counter-AI prompt): CONTESTED. The verdict belongs to this exact sentence only. Whether happiness in families is identifiable depends on subjective criteria and varying definitions of well-being.
tests.notes:
Full reply of P04 (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813, fresh request):

S-001.a	CONTESTED	Whether happiness in families is identifiable depends on subjective criteria and varying definitions of well-being.  
S-001.b	FALSE AS STATED	The claim implies a universal common basis for all happy families, but no such single shared trait or standard has been demonstrated.  
S-002.a	DEMONSTRATED	Unhappiness in families can be identified through observable indicators such as conflict, dysfunction, or distress.  
S-002.b	CONTESTED	The uniqueness of each unhappy family’s situation is plausible but depends on how finely one distinguishes their circumstances.
